What the simulation stands for

Each simulated robot maps to a real, off-the-shelf part list. Tap any image to enlarge.

The idea

Workers sense locally. The Queen thinks globally. A human decides.

👑 Queen: brain and hubHolds the whole map, fuses worker reports, builds the risk map, assigns galleries, talks to the surface and stays near the workers to keep them in radio range.
🐝 Workers: eyes and legsExplore galleries in parallel, detect gas, heat and people locally, send compact reports, and drop relay beacons when the signal fades.
🧑‍✈️ Commander: the gateEvery critical action needs human approval. If the Queen is lost, the workers elect a new one.
Why simulate firstMines are explosive, so failures are rehearsed in a digital twin before any hardware goes underground.

Coordination core validated in simulation (~1,000 fault-injection runs, 0 split-brain) with underwater acoustic parameters; mine-channel re-validation is planned. The circuit shown is a test-bench prototype, not certified for methane atmospheres. Everything on the Simulation tab is scripted and simulated, not measured.
